API¶

FastAPI application¶

The API is implemented in src/api/main.py and exposes the following endpoints.

Endpoint

Purpose

GET /health

Service health check.

GET /summary

Overall dashboard metrics.

GET /vehicles/top?limit=5

Highest-efficiency vehicles.

GET /vehicles/bottom?limit=5

Lowest-efficiency vehicles.

GET /models

Model-level efficiency.

GET /regions

Region-level efficiency.

GET /range-trend

Daily estimated-range trend.

Local data layer¶

src/api/queries.py currently reads curated CSV files from data/curated_local/. This keeps the local application independent of AWS credentials.

For the AWS deployment, the query layer can be replaced with an Athena implementation while preserving the API route structure.

Python API reference¶

FastAPI application exposing EV analytics endpoints.

The API is intentionally thin: route handlers validate request parameters and delegate data retrieval to src.api.queries.

src.api.main.get_bottom(limit: int = fastapi.Query)¶

Return the requested number of bottom-efficiency vehicles.

src.api.main.get_models()¶

Return model efficiency analytics.

src.api.main.get_range_trend()¶

Return the daily range trend.

src.api.main.get_regions()¶

Return region efficiency analytics.

src.api.main.get_summary()¶

Return summary analytics.

src.api.main.get_top(limit: int = fastapi.Query)¶

Return the requested number of top-efficiency vehicles.

src.api.main.health()¶

Return a lightweight health status for service checks.

Local query layer for the FastAPI application.

During local development the API reads curated CSV files generated by the pipeline. In the AWS deployment this layer can be replaced by an Athena query implementation without changing the API route contract.

src.api.queries.bottom_vehicles(limit=5)[source]¶

Return the lowest-efficiency vehicles as API records.

src.api.queries.models()[source]¶

Return model-level efficiency records.

src.api.queries.range_trend()[source]¶

Return daily estimated-range trend records.

src.api.queries.read(name)[source]¶

Read one curated CSV dataset from the local analytics directory.

src.api.queries.regions()[source]¶

Return region-level efficiency records.

src.api.queries.summary()[source]¶

Return dashboard-level summary metrics.

src.api.queries.top_vehicles(limit=5)[source]¶

Return the highest-efficiency vehicles as API records.
